caption:
Elon Musk says he signed a petition asking Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO on November 12.
The Stand with Jensen letter had more than 117,000 names by Saturday afternoon, including about 6,000 people who say they work at Nvidia.
The names are self-reported, and some are clearly fake.

paragraphs.text: Elon Musk said on X on November 13, 2026 that he was signing an online petition calling on Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive. "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," Musk wrote, according to Moneywise. Huang resigned on November 12, and the board named chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO.

The petition, published at standwithjensen.com under the name Stand with Jensen, describes itself as volunteer-run and says it is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nvidia or Huang. Its organizers have not been publicly named in the coverage.

The letter's live counter showed 117,112 names as of 2:03 p.m. Pacific time on November 14, Implicator reported, up from about 108,000 that morning. Signers sorted themselves into 6,019 current Nvidia employees, 1,120 former employees, 63,727 shareholders and 46,246 other supporters. About 77,669 of the names were publicly searchable, because signers can choose to hide theirs.

None of those affiliations are verified. Business Insider and Implicator both found plainly fake entries, including "Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor" and "Xi Jingping," and organizers said on X that they were removing them. Moneywise described the totals as a rough gauge of support. For scale, Moneywise noted that Nvidia reported about 42,000 employees at the end of its last fiscal year.

Names on the public list include Replit chief executive Amjad Masad, Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator chief executive Garry Tan, according to Moneywise and Implicator. Business Insider reported that Musk and Masad promoted the petition on X and that Boom Supersonic chief executive Blake Scholl is also listed.

The letter asks the board to bring Huang back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, to disclose the scope, independence and timeline of that investigation, to give Huang a meaningful chance to respond, and to explain publicly the evidence behind his departure. Organizers argue that he was removed without due process and say they have not been shown evidence supporting the espionage allegation.

Separately, Altimeter Capital chief executive Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management managing partner Gavin Baker wrote to the board on November 13. They praised Kress but asked for a measured search that leaves room for Huang's possible return, warning against what they called a rush to replace him. Altimeter disclosed about 9.4 million Nvidia shares as of June 30, and Atreides about 1.2 million.

The board has not publicly answered the petition or the investor letter. As of November 13 it was still choosing a search firm and had not formally engaged candidates. Independent directors retained the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz on November 10 to run an outside investigation, and director Harvey Jones became the board's first chair.

Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair, and reports have linked him to Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore firm Megaspeed whom U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. China has denied the claim, and Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had reached no conclusions. Neither Huang nor Nvidia has been charged with wrongdoing.

A petition carries no legal weight with Nvidia's board, and its numbers are soft. Its value is as a signal: a public list of employees, shareholders and well-known founders willing to back Huang puts pressure on directors to show how they reached their decision. Moneywise pointed to the 2023 episode in which OpenAI reinstated Sam Altman within days after staff threatened to leave, though Nvidia's situation involves government inquiries that OpenAI's did not.
Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday, November 17, its first earnings call without Huang, and investors will be listening for any comment on the CEO search and the investigation's timeline.
